easy.explanation: Abimelech went to Shechem unto his mother's brethren and the family of his mother's father.
easy.q: To whom did Abimelech go at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: The men gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver.
easy.q: How many pieces of silver did Abimelech receive?

easy.explanation: He slew his seventy brethren upon one stone.
easy.q: What did Abimelech do to his brethren, the sons of Jerubbaal?

answers: He had delivered them from Midian
medium.explanation: They supported Abimelech because they considered him their brother.
medium.q: Why did the hearts of the men of Shechem incline to follow Abimelech?

answers: He hired vain and light persons
medium.explanation: He used the money to hire vain and light persons to follow him.
medium.q: How did Abimelech use the silver he received?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes people of little worth who acted recklessly.
medium.q: What does “vain and light persons” describe?

answers: One ruler would be better than seventy brothers ruling over them
He was the only surviving son of Jerubbaal
He was already king over all Israel
challenge.explanation: He asked whether it was better for seventy sons to reign over them or for one man to reign, reminding them that he was their bone and flesh.
challenge.q: What argument did Abimelech use to persuade the men of Shechem to support him?

challenge.explanation: Jotham was left because he hid himself.
challenge.q: Why was Jotham the only one of Jerubbaal’s sons left alive?

answers: The men of Shechem made him king
challenge.explanation: After the killing of his brothers, the men of Shechem gathered and made Abimelech king.
challenge.q: What was the final step in Abimelech’s rise to power at Shechem?

easy.explanation: Jotham stood in the top of Mount Gerizim and cried to the men of Shechem.
easy.q: From where did Jotham lift up his voice?

easy.explanation: The trees came to the bramble and asked it to reign over them.
easy.q: Which tree was finally chosen as king in the parable?

answers: Put their trust in his shadow
easy.explanation: The bramble said, “Come and put your trust in my shadow.”
easy.q: What did the bramble tell the trees to do?

answers: They preferred to continue producing what benefited others
They did not know the other trees
medium.explanation: Each tree refused to leave its useful fruit and service in order to be promoted over the trees.
medium.q: Why did the olive tree, fig tree, and vine refuse to reign?

answers: He praised them for their choice
He asked whether they had dealt truly and sincerely in making Abimelech king
He told them to choose the olive tree
medium.explanation: Jotham challenged them to consider whether their actions toward Jerubbaal and his house were righteous.
medium.q: How did Jotham connect the parable to the men of Shechem?

medium.explanation: The olive tree’s fatness represents the valuable produce by which it honored God and man.
medium.q: In the olive tree’s words, what does “my fatness” refer to?

answers: A ruler who is useless but threatens others
A leader who protects every tree
A person who refuses all authority
challenge.explanation: The bramble offers little benefit and threatens destruction by fire.
challenge.q: What does the bramble represent in Jotham’s parable?

answers: The trees would receive a greater harvest
Fire could come out of it and devour the cedars of Lebanon
The bramble would become a fruit tree
challenge.explanation: The bramble warned that fire might come out of it and devour even the cedars of Lebanon.
challenge.q: What could happen because of the bramble’s condition?

answers: The men of Shechem forgot how Jerubbaal fought for and delivered them from Midian
Abimelech forgot the men of Thebez
challenge.explanation: Jotham reminded them that his father had fought for them and delivered them from Midian, yet they slew his sons.

paragraphs.title: The Alliance Between Abimelech and Shechem Breaks Down

easy.explanation: Jotham fled to Beer for fear of Abimelech.
Abimelech had reigned three years over Israel.
easy.q: How long did Abimelech reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Gaal son of Ebed came with his brethren, and the men of Shechem put their confidence in him.
easy.q: Who came to Shechem and joined the opposition to Abimelech?

answers: God sent an evil spirit between them
The men of Thebez attacked them
medium.explanation: The text says that God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem.
medium.q: What caused hostility to develop between Abimelech and the men of Shechem?

answers: They set liers in wait and robbed travelers
medium.explanation: They set ambushes in the tops of the mountains and robbed all who passed by.
medium.q: How did the men of Shechem act against Abimelech before Gaal appeared?

answers: People hiding in order to attack
medium.explanation: Liers in wait hide and wait for an opportunity to attack or rob others.

answers: They openly celebrated and cursed Abimelech
challenge.explanation: After gathering and making merry, they went into the house of their god and cursed Abimelech.
challenge.q: What did the feast at the house of their god reveal about the men of Shechem?

answers: The men of Hamor, the father of Shechem
Jotham and the sons of Jerubbaal
challenge.explanation: Gaal asked, “Why should we serve him?” and told them to serve the men of Hamor.
challenge.q: Whom did Gaal suggest the men of Shechem should serve instead of Abimelech?

answers: He confidently challenged Abimelech to come and fight
He asked Abimelech to join him
challenge.explanation: Gaal was challenging Abimelech and inviting him to battle.
challenge.q: What did Gaal mean by, “Increase thine army, and come out”?

paragraphs.title: The Conflict with Gaal and the Defeat of Shechem

easy.explanation: Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard Gaal’s words and his anger was kindled.
easy.q: Who became angry when he heard Gaal’s words?

answers: He lay in wait near Shechem
easy.explanation: Abimelech rose by night and lay in wait in the field near Shechem.
easy.q: What did Abimelech do after receiving Zebul’s message?

answers: He thrust Gaal and his brethren out of Shechem
easy.explanation: Zebul thrust Gaal and his brethren out so that they could not dwell in Shechem.
easy.q: What did Zebul do to Gaal after the battle?

answers: He said they were only the shadow of the mountains
He said they were messengers of peace
He said they were men of Thebez
medium.explanation: Zebul told Gaal, “Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.”
medium.q: How did Zebul explain the people Gaal saw coming down from the mountains?

medium.explanation: He divided the people into three companies.
medium.q: Into how many companies did Abimelech divide his people?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes Abimelech’s company advancing rapidly against the city and its people.
medium.q: What does “rushed forward” describe in the attack?

answers: To warn him that Gaal threatened him and the city
To invite him to a feast
To ask him to leave Shechem
challenge.explanation: Zebul secretly told Abimelech that Gaal and his brethren had come and were fortifying the city against him.
challenge.q: Why did Zebul secretly send messengers to Abimelech?

answers: The city was given to Gaal
He captured the city, slew its people, and beat it down
challenge.explanation: Abimelech fought against the city, took it, slew the people, beat it down, and sowed it with salt.
challenge.q: What was the result of Abimelech’s victory over Shechem?

answers: The complete ruin of the city
A request for peace from its people
challenge.explanation: Sowing Shechem with salt symbolized its destruction and desolation.
challenge.q: What did sowing the city with salt emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of the Tower of Shechem and Thebez

answers: Into the hold of the house of the god Berith
easy.explanation: They entered into an hold of the house of the god Berith.
easy.q: Where did the men of the tower of Shechem flee?

answers: He cut it down and laid it on his shoulder
easy.explanation: Abimelech cut down a bough, carried it on his shoulder, and told his people to do as he had done.
easy.q: What did Abimelech do with a bough from the trees?

easy.explanation: A certain woman cast a piece of a millstone upon Abimelech’s head.

answers: They burned the hold and killed those inside
medium.explanation: They set the hold on fire, and about a thousand men and women died.
medium.q: What did Abimelech and his people do to the men in the tower of Shechem?

answers: So people would not say that a woman slew him
To prove that he was not wounded
medium.explanation: He feared that people would say, “A woman slew him.”
medium.q: Why did Abimelech ask his armourbearer to kill him?

medium.explanation: The KJV calls it a piece of a millstone, thrown from the tower.
medium.q: What was the piece of a millstone that struck Abimelech?

answers: In both places he attacked a tower where people had taken refuge
In both places he fled from the city
In both places he was made king
challenge.explanation: At both locations Abimelech attacked fortified towers where people had gathered for safety.
challenge.q: What was similar about Abimelech’s actions at Shechem and Thebez?

answers: The wound to Abimelech’s head led to his death
The people of the city surrendered
challenge.explanation: After the woman wounded him, Abimelech was killed by his young armourbearer.
challenge.q: What brought the campaign at Thebez to an end?

answers: Every man departed unto his place
challenge.explanation: The men of Israel departed every man unto his place.
challenge.q: What did the people of Israel do when they saw that Abimelech was dead?

easy.explanation: God rendered the wickedness of Abimelech, which he had done in slaying his brethren.
easy.q: To whom did God render Abimelech’s wickedness?

answers: They aided Abimelech in killing his brethren
easy.explanation: The men of Shechem aided Abimelech in the killing of his brethren.
easy.q: What evil did the men of Shechem commit according to the chapter’s conclusion?

easy.explanation: The chapter says that the curse of Jotham came upon them.
easy.q: What came upon Abimelech and the men of Shechem at the end?

answers: The slaying of his seventy brethren
medium.explanation: The text specifically mentions his slaying of his seventy brethren.
medium.q: Which evil of Abimelech is specifically mentioned in the conclusion?

answers: It brings about the fulfillment of his curse
It proves Abimelech was a righteous king
medium.explanation: The judgment on Abimelech and Shechem fulfills Jotham’s curse.
medium.q: How does God’s judgment relate to Jotham’s words?

answers: God repaid them for the evil they had done
God removed them from the city
medium.explanation: The expression means that God brought their own evil back upon them.
medium.q: What does “God rendered upon their heads” mean?

answers: Those who use violence against others may eventually suffer the consequences themselves
Those who flee always return victorious
A ruler always receives protection from his people
challenge.explanation: Abimelech killed his brothers with Shechem’s support, and the evil was later repaid upon both parties.
challenge.q: What principle of justice appears at the end of the chapter?

answers: Both shared in the wicked deeds
challenge.explanation: Abimelech slew the brothers, and the men of Shechem aided him in that evil.
challenge.q: Why are Abimelech and the men of Shechem mentioned together in the conclusion?

answers: The destructive ruler harms both himself and his supporters
The parable was only about harvests
challenge.explanation: The bramble’s threat of fire is fulfilled symbolically as Abimelech and his supporters destroy one another.
challenge.q: How does the ending deepen the meaning of Jotham’s parable?
